title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Payroll Administrator

The Role

The Payroll Administrator supports the Payroll Officer and Payroll Manager in the accurate and timely processing of payroll, ensuring all employees are paid correctly and statutory payroll obligations are met. The role is responsible for providing efficient administrative support to the payroll function, maintaining accurate records, and assisting with payroll-related queries. In addition, the postholder will provide cover and support across the team during periods of annual leave or absence to ensure the smooth and continuous operation of the department.

Key Responsibilities

P11d System
- Recording and maintenance of data held in the P11d system.
- Be the point of contact for both internal and external queries in relation to the system and the data within it.
- Provide the required monthly reports to Finance.
- Carry out any ad-hoc tasks in the system.
- Take ownership of the Van Declaration forms, ensuring they are received and recorded correctly.

WebExpenses

- Maintain the data in the system to ensure accuracy (cost centre changes, approver changes, etc.).
- Clean the data in the system as a starting point to ensure correct recording going forward.
- Be the point of contact for account queries.

The Guild

- Produce the data for Finance and pass this over every week.
- Be the point of contact for The Guild and the people paid through them.

Court Order Payments
- Raise the payments each month for the court orders processed through the weekly and monthly payrolls.
- Ensure the records kept are accurate and up to date.

Other
- Cover the weekly payroll when the need arises.

Essential:
- Excellent time management skills and the ability to keep to deadlines in an often-challenging environment
- The ability to multi-task with excellent organisational skills
- Experience and proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel
- An eye for detail to ensure accuracy of all information
- Ability to work confidentially with sensitive information

Desireable:

Caring and investing in you

As a Gold Investors in People company and a Sunday Times 100 Best Company to Work For, we are committed to investing in people. title: Accounts Administrator
description:
The Role

- Maintain accurate supplier records and purchase ledger accounts.

Banking & General Accounts
- Post and reconcile bank transactions using Sage 200.
- Update cash records and assist with routine cash-flow reporting.
- Reconcile company credit cards, petty cash and associated expenses.
- Prepare regular sales and purchase ledger reports.
- Assist with external audits and routine financial administration.

Essential Requirements
- Previous experience in a transactional accounting, Accounts Technician or similar finance position.
- Good working knowledge of sales ledger, purchase ledger and credit control procedures.
- Experience preparing bank and supplier reconciliations.
- A good understanding of routine accounting principles and VAT.

Desirable Experience
- AAT qualified or currently studying towards an accounting qualification.
- Experience using Sage 200.
- Knowledge of invoice discounting or factoring arrangements.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary, dependent on experience.
- Generous employer pension contributions.
- Death-in-service life assurance.

title: Credit Controller
description:
As a Credit Controller in Wolverhampton, you will manage credit control activity within the Not For Profit sector, helping the Accounting & Finance department maintain clear and accurate account records. - Ability to organise workload and manage follow-up activity effectively.
- Experience of working with financial records or customer account information.

Job Offer
- Permanent Credit Controller position based in Wolverhampton.
- Salary of £27,000 to £28,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Hybrid working, with 2 days on site.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller

Location: Wolverhampton (Hybrid Working)
Salary: £28,000 - £33,000 DOE
Contract: Permanent
Hours: 37.5 hours per week

The Opportunity

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Senior Credit Controller to join a successful and growing business based in Wolverhampton. This is a key role within the finance team, offering the chance to take ownership of a sizeable customer ledger while working closely with both internal stakeholders and external customers to maximise cash collection and minimise aged debt.

We are looking for a confident and professional credit professional who can build strong relationships, challenge appropriately when required, and help drive continuous improvement across the credit control function.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage and maintain your own customer ledger, ensuring accounts remain up to date.
- Proactively chase outstanding debt via telephone, email and written correspondence.
- Work closely with customers to resolve invoice disputes, purchase order issues and portal-related queries.
- Build strong relationships with key customers to ensure timely payment of invoices.
- Record and maintain accurate customer interaction notes within the credit control system.
- Provide copy invoices, statements and supporting documentation when required.
- Liaise regularly with sales, invoicing and operational teams to resolve outstanding account issues.
- Monitor aged debt and escalate concerns to management where appropriate.
- Conduct credit risk assessments and undertake credit checks on customers.
- Process credit card payments as required.
- Produce monthly cash flow forecasting and debtor reporting.
- Support the implementation of best practice credit control procedures and processes.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous credit control experience within a B2 B environment.
- Strong communication and negotiation skills with the confidence to engage with customers at all levels.
- Experience managing high-value or complex customer accounts.
- A proactive approach to resolving payment disputes and reducing aged debt.
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Strong Excel and reporting skills.
- Experience using finance or ERP systems, ideally including Business Central, Sage 200 or similar platforms.
- Commercial awareness and the ability to balance customer relationships with business objectives.

Key Performance Measures
- Reduce aged debt over 90 days to agreed targets.
- Maintain debtor days (DSO) in line with business objectives.
- Deliver accurate monthly cash flow forecasts.
- Ensure all overdue accounts are actively managed and escalated where necessary.
- Minimise bad debt exposure through effective credit control and risk management.
